seoTitle: Free HTTP Headers to JSON Converter Online
metaDescription: Convert raw HTTP request or response headers, with or without a status line, into a JSON object. Repeated headers become arrays. Free, in-browser.
intro: Paste raw HTTP headers, optionally with a status or request line, and get a JSON object. Repeated headers such as Set-Cookie become arrays.
why:
Headers copied from browser developer tools, curl -i output or a log are plain text lines, while test code, mock servers and API clients want a JSON object. Retyping each line into quotes and commas is dull and gets cookies and folded lines wrong.

This converter reads each Name: value line, keeps the value after the first colon intact, joins folded continuation lines, and turns repeated headers into an array so no Set-Cookie is lost. A leading status line such as HTTP/1.1 200 OK, or a request line such as GET /path HTTP/1.1, is stored under _status. You can lowercase names to match how HTTP/2 shows them. It only converts format and does not interpret the headers.
howTo: Paste the raw headers, with or without the first status line.
Tick lowercase names if you want HTTP/2 style keys.
Copy the JSON object into your test or tool.

faq.q: What happens to headers that appear twice?
faq.a: They become an array of values in the order they appear. This matters for Set-Cookie, which must not be merged into one comma-separated line.

faq.q: Where does the status line go?
faq.a: Into a key called _status at the top of the object, for both response lines like HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found and request lines like POST /api HTTP/1.1.
Yes. A line starting with whitespace is treated as a continuation of the previous header and is joined to it with a single space.

faq.q: What if a line has no colon?
faq.a: The tool stops with an error quoting the line, so a stray body line or a bad copy is easy to find. Remove the body before converting.
